subject: Request: Unwind credit bucket & opt-out language for Veridian pilot
messages:
From: Nora Blake <nora.blake@veridian.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian Legal <legal@veridian.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot contract: request for downsell protections and opt-out language

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the quick demo this week — the engineers were impressed. Before we sign the pilot SOW we'd like to confirm two items that are blockers for procurement:

1) Downsell protections: we'd like a clear mechanism if usage falls below 30% of committed throughput after month 2. Ideally a path to scale down capacity without an early termination penalty — either pro-rated credits or a structured credit bucket.

2) Opt-out clause: procurement needs a one-time opt-out window within the first 45 days tied to measurable onboarding milestones (latency < 300ms for key routes and API integration test passing). If milestones aren't met, Veridian wants ability to step down with limited financial exposure.

We can accept a modest discount in exchange for these protections, but we need the legal language and a simple matrix so our CFO can sign off. Can your team share proposed amendment language and any precedent?

I can loop in legal, but wanted to start with you.

Cheers,
Nora
Nora Blake
Director, Platform Partnerships
Veridian.ai

Attachment: onboarding_metrics_template.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian Legal <legal@veridian.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot contract: request for downsell protections and opt-out language

Hi Marcus / Laura — forwarding Veridian's ask. TL;DR: they want a structured way to step down (no full early-termination penalty) if adoption lags, plus a one-time opt-out tied to onboarding milestones. They are willing to take a modest discount.

Proposed internal approach (first pass):
- Create a 3-month credit bucket equal to 20% of monthly committed spend that can be applied against months 3-6 if usage drops below threshold.
- Make the opt-out a single 45-day window starting at go-live; opt-out triggers return to pay-as-you-go pricing with the credit bucket applied, no further termination fee.
- Require two objective milestones (latency and integration test) to qualify the opt-out.

I've attached a draft amendment (proposed_unwind_amendment_v1.pdf) and the updated SOW. Would like executive ok on the credit bucket size and whether Legal can proceed with that clause.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Chen
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ava — good summary. A few thoughts and a suggested conservative template for sign-off so we don't set a broad precedent: 

- Credit bucket: propose 15% of monthly committed ARR, applied as credits over the following three months if usage falls below 30% of committed throughput for any sustained 30-day window after month 2. This is smaller than your 20% suggestion but keeps economics predictable.
- Opt-out window: approve a single 45-day window. Opt-out triggers transition to PAYG rates for the remainder of the original term; the credit bucket is applied immediately to offset the first two months of post-opt-out invoices. No refunds beyond credits.
- Milestones: agree to the two objective checks (latency and integration tests). Legal should require logs and the integration test report as evidence.
- Discount: we can offer a 7.5% one-time onboarding discount for the first billing cycle if they sign with the above protections.

I've attached a redline in the PDF (proposed_unwind_amendment_v1.pdf) and a short example billing worksheet. Laura / Markus — need executive confirmation that 15% credit bucket + 7.5% onboarding discount is acceptable to finalize with Legal and Sales Ops.

-Marcus

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot contract: request for downsell protections and opt-out language

Okay to proceed with Marcus' recommendation with two constraints:
1) Cap the aggregate exposure (credit bucket + onboarding discount) at no more than 18% of the three-month committed value — that keeps the finance impact bounded.
2) Legal to include a narrow carve-out: opt-out is only available once and only if Veridian provides the integration test report and 14 days of route-level latency metrics showing the failing SLA. No subjective language.

If Legal can implement those two guardrails in the amendment, Ava you have executive approval to finalize and send to Veridian for sign-off. Keep me in the loop if we need an exception to the cap.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
